title: Analytic Lines, Negative-Reciprocal Perpendicularity, and the Section Formula
subtitle: Exact rational slopes, 90-degree rotation of slope triangles, and weighted division of directed segments.
challenge: Rotating a right triangle with horizontal run dx and vertical rise dy by 90 degrees swaps its legs and reverses one direction: (dx, dy) becomes (-dy, dx). How does this single geometric rotation immediately prove that perpendicular non-vertical lines satisfy m_1 * m_2 = -1?
predictionPrompt: Line L is perpendicular to y = (3/4)x + 2 and passes through the point (6, 5). What is the exact y-intercept b of line L?
formalDefinition: Through any two distinct points A(x_1, y_1) and B(x_2, y_2) with x_1 != x_2, the slope is the invariant ratio m = (y_2 - y_1)/(x_2 - x_1). Two non-vertical lines with slopes m_1, m_2 are parallel iff m_1 = m_2 and perpendicular iff m_1 m_2 = -1 (so m_perp = -1/m_1). Moreover, the unique point P dividing the directed segment AB internally in the ratio AP : PB = m : n has coordinates P = ((n x_1 + m x_2)/(m + n), (n y_1 + m y_2)/(m + n)).

steps: Task: Find the equation and y-intercept of the line perpendicular to y = (3/4)x + 2 through (6, 5), and find the x-coordinate of P dividing A(-2, 1) to B(8, 6) in the ratio 2 : 3.
The given line has slope m_1 = 3/4, so the perpendicular slope is the negative reciprocal m_perp = -4/3.
For P dividing A(-2, 1) to B(8, 6) in ratio m : n = 2 : 3, apply the section formula: x_P = (3(-2) + 2(8)) / (2 + 3) = (-6 + 16)/5 = 10/5 = 2.
workedExample.result: Perpendicular y-intercept b = 13; section point coordinate x_P = 2.

misconception.mistake: Taking the reciprocal without negating (+q/p instead of -q/p) for perpendicular slope, or failing to cross-weight the endpoints (computing m*x_1 + n*x_2 instead of n*x_1 + m*x_2) in the section formula.
misconception.correction: A positive-sloped line rises to the right, so any line perpendicular to it must fall to the right (negative slope): m_perp = -q/p. In the section formula, when m is small (P is close to A), x_1 must receive the larger weight n.

reflection: Notice that the familiar midpoint formula M = ((x_1 + x_2)/2, (y_1 + y_2)/2) is simply the special case m : n = 1 : 1 of the internal section formula.
prerequisiteCheck: Compute the rise y_2 - y_1 and run x_2 - x_1 from A(-3, 4) to B(2, -6).
representation: Draw the slope right triangle (dx, dy) on a line and rotate that triangle 90 degrees counterclockwise to (-dy, dx) to see why rise/run becomes -run/rise.

faded.prompt: Find the x-coordinate of P dividing A(1, 3) to B(11, 8) in the ratio 3 : 2: x_P = (2(1) + 3(11)) / (3 + 2) = (2 + __) / 5 = __.

independent.prompt: Find the exact slope of the line passing through (-4, 7) and (2, -2).
Find the exact y-intercept b of the line perpendicular to y = (2/5)x - 1 that passes through (4, 3).

explanation: Why do the weights n and m swap positions in the numerator n x_1 + m x_2 of the section formula when AP : PB = m : n?

transfer.prompt: Prove using the section formula that the centroid G of a triangle with vertices A(x_1, y_1), B(x_2, y_2), C(x_3, y_3)—located 2/3 of the way from A to the midpoint M of BC (ratio AG : GM = 2 : 1)—has x-coordinate (x_1 + x_2 + x_3)/3.
transfer.solution: The midpoint M of BC has x_M = (x_2 + x_3)/2. Dividing AM in ratio m : n = 2 : 1 gives x_G = (1 * x_1 + 2 * ((x_2 + x_3)/2)) / (2 + 1) = (x_1 + x_2 + x_3)/3.

retrieval: State the slope formula, the algebraic condition for two non-vertical lines to be perpendicular, and the internal section formula for ratio m : n.
